name: Thymosin Fraction 5

lead: Thymosin fraction 5 is a calf-thymus extract made in 1972 by Allan Goldstein's group, containing dozens of peptides. Thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were later purified from it. It matters to this wiki as the origin of peptides that people use for recovery and healthier ageing.

The extract restored immune function in thymus-deficient animals, which led to the idea of thymic hormones. Clinical work focuses on purified thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin) in infection and cancer, not on the extract for appearance.

paras: It is rarely used directly; people in thymic-peptide discussions generally use the purified peptides instead.
No approved use of the extract was found, and no appearance-related safety data. Animal-derived mixtures vary in composition.

angle.text: Thymosin fraction 5 is the calf-thymus extract from which thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were purified. It shows up in thymic-peptide discussions as the source of those peptides; no appearance use is documented.

lead: Thymosin fraction 5 (TF5) is a partially purified extract of calf thymus prepared in 1972 by Allan Goldstein's group, which contains many small peptides, including the later-characterized thymosin alpha-1 and thymosin beta-4 [1][2][3][1]. It was the starting material from which individual thymosins were purified.

Its relevance to looksmaxxing is indirect: it appears in thymic peptide and longevity discussions as the origin of the peptides sold as research chemicals. Published clinical work focuses on purified thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin) in infection and cancer, not on TF5 for appearance [4][5].

paras: Work on thymic extracts began in the 1960s with Abraham White and then Goldstein, who showed that extracts restored immune function in animals lacking a thymus [2][6]. TF5 was reported to contain over 40 peptides of roughly 1,000 to 15,000 Da, grouped as alpha, beta and gamma thymosins; they are structurally unrelated, and some are widespread in tissues rather than thymus-specific [6].

Thymosin alpha-1 was isolated and sequenced in 1977 and 1979 [3][7][8], and bovine thymosin beta-4 was sequenced in 1981 [1]. Later work found that alpha-1 derives from a larger precursor, prothymosin alpha [9].

No studies of crude TF5 as an appearance intervention were found. Related clinical work concerns thymosin treatment of chronic hepatitis B in a placebo-controlled pilot trial in 1991 [10] and registered phase 2 trials of thymosin alpha-1 (thymalfasin) in cancer settings [4][5][11]. Laboratory work has also reported effects of thymic hormones on natural killer cell activity [12].
TF5 itself is not a typical consumer product; purified peptides derived from it are what appear in research-peptide markets. No approved use of the extract was found.
